info.title: Tiducto Transit API — Stops
info.description: Stop text/geo search — a plain-REST customer surface (key-auth). Companion to routing and realtime; the three share one pack version. `locationType` and `wheelchairBoarding` are GTFS integer codes, not enums, so an unrecognized code passes through unchanged.

servers.description: Your environment. Replace `{env-slug}` with your environment's slug.

4XX.description: Stop-search error: a 400 whose message names the field when `limit` is missing, not an integer or out of range, or the body has a key it doesn't accept; or a search error such as filtering a non-filterable attribute.

403.description: Forbidden — the key is not permitted for this operation.

apikey.name: apikey
apikey.description: The raw key in an `apikey` header (not Authorization: Bearer).

StopSearchRequest.description: POST body for `/stops/search`. The body accepts only `q`, `filter`, `sort` and `limit`; any other key is an HTTP 400 naming that key. `filter` and `sort` are search-index expressions the client composes (not modeled shapes). Filterable `StopHit` fields: `gtfsId`, the admin levels (`country`, `region`, `district`, `city`, `suburb`), `locationType`, `wheelchairBoarding` and `modes`; `_geo` (the stop's position) is filterable and sortable. The other `StopHit` fields (`name`, `code`, `lat`, `lon`) aren't filterable, and a filter on one of them fails with a `StopSearchError`. Filtering on an admin level the environment wasn't enriched with matches no stops rather than failing.

q.description: Search text, matched against the stop's `name`, its `code`, its town (`city`) and the district within the town (`suburb`); town and district only where the environment has them.

filter.description: Search filter expression. Supports admin-level equality (e.g. `city = "Brno"`), by-id lookup (`gtfsId = "1:39822"`), stop kind (`locationType = 1` for stations; `locationType != 1` for everything else, which also matches stops that omit the field), accessibility (`wheelchairBoarding = 1`), mode (`modes = RAIL` for stops a rail route serves), radius (`_geoRadius(lat, lng, meters)`), and bounding box (`_geoBoundingBox([maxLat, maxLng], [minLat, minLng])`). Combine multiple with ` AND `.

sort.description: Sort expressions, e.g. ["_geoPoint(lat, lng):asc"] to order by distance (nearest-stop). Requires _geo (present).

limit.description: Max hits to return, an integer from 1 to 50. A missing, non-integer or out-of-range value is an HTTP 400 naming `limit`.

StopHit.description: One stop. A station's platforms are folded into it, so the station is returned instead of its platforms. Admin levels are populated only where the deployment enriched them; the other optional fields are absent when the feed doesn't provide them. A hit can carry further fields not listed here; they aren't part of the contract and may change or disappear, so ignore them.

gtfsId.description: Feed-prefixed stop id (`<feedId>:<id>`), the same id routing's `gtfsId` carries.

code.description: Short public code riders know the stop by, as the feed gives it (GTFS `stop_code`), e.g. the one printed on its sign.

locationType.description: GTFS `location_type`: `0` a stop or platform, `1` a station (its platforms folded into it). Absent when the feed doesn't set it, which means a stop. No other values are returned.

wheelchairBoarding.description: GTFS `wheelchair_boarding`: `1` some vehicles here can be boarded by a rider in a wheelchair, `2` wheelchair boarding isn't possible here, `0` no information. A station's value is the station's own; its platforms' values aren't combined into it. Absent when the feed doesn't set it, which also means no information. Any other value is passed through from the feed unchanged.

modes.description: Modes of the routes serving the stop, each once, sorted: the mode names routing returns for those routes (e.g. `BUS`, `TRAM`, `RAIL`). A station's modes cover all its platforms. Absent when no route serves the stop.

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error body: a stable machine-readable `code` and a human-readable `message`.
